central_reading: Self-awareness is the nature (svabhāva) of consciousness, not a result (phala) of cognition. The Buddhist svasaṃvitti doctrine treats self-awareness as the result of cognition; Abhinavagupta argues this makes it derivative rather than intrinsic.

nyaya_reading.paksa: self-awareness is the nature of consciou
nyaya_reading.hetu: consciousness is self-luminous and its own object, not dependent on external means of knowledge
nyaya_reading.sadhya: self-awareness is the nature of consciousness, not a produced result
nyaya_reading.vyapti: If consciousness is self-luminous and self-aware by nature, then self-awareness

nnexpr_mappings.falsifier: Show that the Buddhist phala-model of svasaṃvitti is compatible with svaprakāśa — that a result-of-cognition can also be the nature of consciousness without contradiction.

argument_edges.relation_rationale: Direct textual evidence distinguishing svabhāva from phala models.
The Buddhist phala-model makes self-awareness derivative.
